content.value_statement: Teams need reliable ways to create focused AI agents without misconfiguring tools or prompts. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users through structured agent definitions.
actual_capabilities: Guides quick creation of project-level or user-level Claude Code agents.
Explains required agent frontmatter fields, descriptions, tool lists, and model choices.
Provides interview-style prompts for clarifying agent purpose, triggers, inputs, and outputs.
Includes examples for reviewers, test runners, researchers, and implementation agents.
References Task tool usage, parallel delegation, hooks, slash commands, and MCP integration patterns.
limitations: It creates guidance and agent definition content, not a running agent service.
Generated agents still need human review before they receive write, shell, or network tools.
It is focused on Claude Code agent patterns and may need adaptation for other tools.
It does not validate every generated agent against a live project automatically.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Agents
use_cases.description: Create shared project agents with consistent descriptions, tool scopes, and review workflows.

use_cases.title: Build Personal Automation Helpers
use_cases.description: Define user-level agents for repeated coding, research, testing, or documentation tasks.

use_cases.title: Create Read-Only Review Agents
use_cases.description: Design focused reviewers that inspect code without write access or broad shell permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Reviewer
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-factory to create a read-only code reviewer for Python changes. Ask only for missing essentials and suggest a safe tool scope.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Test Runner
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test-runner agent for this repository. Include when to invoke it, required tools, a diagnosis workflow, and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Interview for a Research Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use interview mode to design a technology research agent. Help me choose its model, storage location, tools, and report structure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three related Claude Code agents for review, implementation, and verification. Define boundaries, handoffs, and minimum tool access for each.

output_examples.input: Create a test runner agent for a TypeScript project.
output: A project-level test-runner agent with clear activation rules and a focused test workflow.
The agent uses scoped read, edit, shell, and search tools only when they are needed.
The output format includes test results, failure analysis, proposed fixes, and verification status.

output_examples.input: Build a read-only security reviewer agent.
output: A reviewer agent focused on authentication, authorization, secrets, injection, and unsafe file handling.
The tool scope avoids write and shell access, so the agent can inspect code without modifying it.
The review report is organized by severity, evidence, impact, and recommended fixes.

output_examples.input: Help me decide where to store a new agent.
output: A recommendation based on whether the agent is personal, project-specific, or shared with a team.
The answer explains precedence between project-level and user-level agents in simple terms.

best_practices: Start with one clear responsibility before adding tools or complex workflows.
Use the minimum tool scope that lets the agent complete its assigned job.
Test new agents on realistic tasks and revise prompts when outputs are vague.
anti_patterns: Do not give every new agent full shell, write, and network access by default.
Do not combine unrelated duties into one broad general-purpose agent.
Do not skip the description field, because activation quality depends on it.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code agent definition files with frontmatter, prompts, tool scopes, and usage guidance.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides agent definition and usage. The user still decides when to invoke an agent.

faq.question: Can it create project-level and user-level agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains both storage locations and when each location is appropriate.

faq.question: How should tool access be chosen?
faq.answer: Start with the smallest set of tools required for the agent purpose, then expand only when needed.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: The instructions are written for Claude Code agent files, but the design practices can inform Claude and Codex workflows.

faq.question: What should I review before using a generated agent?
faq.answer: Review its description, tool list, model choice, workflow steps, and boundaries before using it on real project work.
